fields.sections.0.h: X Corp's Demand for Forced Shutdown
fields.sections.1.h: Service Resumption Declaration After Legal Review
fields.sections.0.ko: On August 24, 2026, X Corp sent a legal notice demanding permanent shutdown of all Nitter instances and project repositories. This indicates X will not tolerate users accessing content without going through Twitter's official frontend. The incident demonstrates how strictly social media platforms control data access.
fields.sections.1.ko: Following the shutdown demand, Nitter project developers sought legal advice and decided to continue the project. They made a simple declaration, "Following legal advice, the Nitter project will continue," and indicated that more detailed information would be released soon. This decision was made under the judgment of legal experts rather than through purely technical or ethical resistance.
fields.sections.2.ko: Nitter is an open-source privacy-focused alternative frontend to Twitter. All requests pass through a backend, preventing direct client communication with Twitter, thus preventing user IP tracking and JavaScript fingerprinting. It uses an unofficial API without requiring developer accounts and is lightweight at 60KB compared to the official website's 784KB.
fields.sections.3.ko: During README updates, RSS feed functionality was added but has been disabled on many instances due to abuse. Meanwhile, embed functionality was removed, with separate guide documentation provided. This reflects the project's evolution in balancing technical stability and security.
fields.sections.4.ko: Beyond traditional platform support through GitHub Sponsors, Patreon, Liberapay, and Ko-fi, the project also provides various cryptocurrency wallet addresses including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Monero, Solana, and Zcash. This can be interpreted as a strategy to continuously secure funding amid legal threats.
fields.sections.5.ko: A new item "For legal inquiries and DMCA requests, contact legal@poast.org" has been added to the README's contact section. This indicates that Nitter developers have established a dedicated response system for legal matters, suggesting that future disputes will be handled in a structured manner rather than randomly.
fields.caveat: This material is provided in GitHub commit message form and does not include detailed evidence or final determinations regarding Nitter's legal position or the outcome of the dispute with X Corp.
